title: Rust gateway forwards multicast across backbone; BR multicast drop (spec 04 6.3.4) missing
description: Spec 04-network.md 6.3.4: Border routers MUST NOT forward mesh multicasts to the internet; multicast dropped in both directions (mesh→internet and internet→mesh) unless explicitly configured multicast peering. Classification: divergent (stack split). Evidence: C implemented+tested — lichen/subsys/lichen/routing/router.c:576-589 drops backbone-ingress multicast unless packet->multicast_peering (router.h:146); test lichen/tests/routing_dispatch/src/main.c:277-284. Python implemented+tested — python/src/lichen/routing/router.py:493-499 (is_border_router + is_multicast + not multicast_peering_enabled → DROP), 8 tests python/tests/routing/test_router.py:469-597. Rust gateway MISSING the filter: upstream_to_mesh (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:1539-1558) checks only ULA 0xfd then is_local_mesh — a multicast destination falls through to transmit_ipv6_wire (:1556), so internet→mesh multicast is transmitted onto the LoRa mesh; forward_mesh_to_upstream (rust/lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs:914-956) TUN-writes non-local destinations including multicast, so mesh→internet multicast reaches the backbone; the RPL stack accepts multicast destinations as deliverable (rust/lichen-node/src/stack.rs:587-595, 795-806). No multicast_peering or 6.3.4 reference under rust/. Suggested placement: add 0xff multicast drop to upstream_to_mesh and forward_mesh_to_upstream with a multicast_peering config flag mirroring C router.h:146; add gateway end_to_end tests for both directions. Sweep ref R-04-007.
close_reason: Rust gateway now enforces the spec 04 6.3.4 BR multicast boundary, matching the C and Python reference behavior: Gateway gained multicast_peering (bool, default FALSE = drop) with set_multicast_peering/multicast_peering_enabled accessors mirroring C router.h:146; upstream_to_mesh (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs) drops backbone→mesh multicast (dst[0]==0xff) after the ULA check before local-mesh/wire routing; forward_mesh_to_upstream (src/bin/lichend.rs) drops mesh→backbone multicast after the local-mesh branch and before the TUN write. Silent drop (no ICMPv6 error) matches C/Python. New end_to_end test upstream_multicast_dropped_without_multicast_peering: default-off drops ff02::1a echo, peering-enabled forwards. Verification: full lichen-gateway suite 11/11 result blocks green, clippy clean for touched files (a pre-existing too-many-arguments warning in lichen-node/src/secure.rs:642 is kpv0.6 lint-debt, unaffected), fmt clean. Backbone-crossing audit: the only transmit sites are the two guarded paths (gateway.rs:1582 wire, lichend.rs:955 TUN) plus mesh-internal delivery — no bypass. Codereview: correctness pass by Kimi K3 — PASS with one P3 (peering-ON path lacks C's scope>=3/hop_limit>1 relay gating and forwarded_hop_limit) filed as worker6-iidb (latent: no production caller sets the flag); security + edge-case passes timed out twice (reviewer latency), completed via worker-loop fallback self-review: backbone-crossing audit clean, flag has no production setter (default-off enforced), silent-drop parity confirmed, <40-byte ipv6 reaching TUN pre-existing (ingress produces full headers), peering-ON path exercises rule-255 fallback for multicast dst successfully.
